tex_content.html:
\begin{equation} \Ric _{g_\infty (t)}+\Hess ^{g_\infty (t)}f(t) +\frac1{2t}g_\infty (t)=0. \end{equation} The limit has nonnegative curvature operator, is $\kappa $-non-collapsed, and satisfies $\partial _tR\geq 0$.
Proof

\sketch The estimates and compactness argument are recorded in Claims 3–3. The pulled-back reduced lengths converge to $l_\infty $; the distributional argument culminating in Proposition 2.3 makes this limit smooth. Proposition 2.7 then gives Equation 2. Finally, Claim 2.8 and the strict reduced-volume bound rule out a flat limit.

□
